name: Green Peas
perishability: Highly perishable. Pods wilt in 2–3 days; peas lose sweetness within hours unless cooled.
summary: A short winter crop of the North Indian plains, with a summer crop from the Himalaya. The January–February glut is huge, and frozen-pea makers buy heavily then to sell through the year. Prices are highest in September–November, when only hill and early crops reach the market.

key_numbers.label: Crop duration
key_numbers.note: early varieties like Arkel in ~60 days

key_numbers.label: Price swing
key_numbers.note: ₹100–200/kg in Oct vs ₹10–20/kg in Feb (retail, typical)

global: India is the second-largest green pea producer. Frozen peas are a growing processed market; India also imports dry (field) peas for dal, a separate market.

states.basis: Major producing states (ranked approximately; shares not shown)

belts.name: Jabalpur
belts.note: One of the largest pea markets; early winter crop.

belts.name: Doaba
belts.note: Early winter peas for Delhi and processors.

belts.name: Himachal hills
belts.note: Off-season peas Jun–Oct at premium prices.

seasons.name: Plains winter
seasons.region: UP, MP, Punjab, Haryana, Bihar, Jharkhand

seasons.name: Hills summer
seasons.note: The only fresh supply through the monsoon.

climate.v: Cool season, 10–22 °C. Heat above ~25 °C at flowering cuts pod set.
Plants tolerate light frost, but frost at flowering and pod fill damages the crop.
Light irrigation; waterlogging causes root rot.

weather_risks.risk: Frost and cold wave at flowering

weather_risks.impact: Short pod-fill period; hard, starchy peas.
Blocked roads cut the off-season supply.
Delays sowing and shifts the harvest.

pests.name: Powdery mildew
pests.impact: Most common disease; heavy in late-sown crops.

postharvest.respiration: Non-climacteric, high respiration; sugars turn to starch quickly when warm.
practices: Pods are picked when bright green and well filled; sold in 40–50 kg bags.
Frozen-pea plants shell and blanch peas within hours of harvest during the Jan–Feb glut.
Shelled fresh peas sell at 2–3 times the pod price per kg (shelling yield is ~40–50%).

steps.what: Hand-picked pods, bagged in the field.
Auction at Jabalpur, Barabanki, Jalandhar; contract supply to freezing plants.
Pods by the kg, shelled peas, and frozen peas year-round.

supply_chain.farmer_share: Not estimated in the RBI series.

varieties.name: Pusa Pragati, Kashi Nandini, Kashi Uday, Punjab-89

trade.exports: Small fresh exports; some frozen peas.
trade.imports: Fresh negligible. Dry (yellow) peas imports are a separate pulses market.

policy.what: No MSP for green peas; dry-pea import rules affect pulses, not fresh peas.

history.what: Only hill and early peas; retail ₹100–200/kg.

signals: Sowing progress in UP and MP (Oct–Nov).
Frost and cold-wave forecasts for Punjab, Haryana and UP (Dec–Jan).
business: Frozen peas are a clear processing play: buy in the February glut, sell all year.
Shelled fresh peas carry large mark-ups on quick commerce (₹510/kg peeled vs ₹200/kg in pod on Blinkit Delhi).
Hill peas in the monsoon are a premium sourcing window.
